sections.name: settings
sections.notes: All active writable settings emitted by the current Smithproxy saver are typed and editable with ranges aligned to the pinned upstream schema. OCSP and CRL status TTLs remain visible but read-only because upstream marks them VALUE_NONE. Integer quotas accept the full lossless JSON range. HTTP API and webhook identities, endpoints, bind targets, administration identity, filesystem paths, credentials, API keys, syslog targets, filename components, and rating keys use write-only replace/clear controls. Deprecated thread-spray tuning keys are accepted and ignored by Smithproxy and are intentionally not exposed.

sections.name: debug
sections.notes: Global debug flags and the current per-module boolean, integer, and bounded string logging overrides are typed and editable. Module names are constrained to draft-path-safe identifiers.

sections.name: address_objects
sections.notes: The pinned Smithproxy schema supports CIDR and FQDN address objects only; both are represented by typed edit and structural create drawers. Confirmed structural deletion is available only for objects without live or pending policy/routing references and without pending field edits. Structural operations remain capability-gated on stable entity IDs.

sections.name: port_objects
sections.notes: Port ranges are represented by typed edit and structural create drawers. Creation validates ascending bounded ranges; confirmed deletion is limited to objects without live or pending policy/routing references and without pending field edits. Structural operations remain capability-gated on stable entity IDs.

sections.name: proto_objects
sections.notes: Protocol identifiers are represented by typed edit and structural create drawers. Creation validates unique protocol numbers in the Smithproxy-supported range 1-255; confirmed deletion is limited to objects without live or pending policy references and without pending field edits. Structural operations remain capability-gated on stable entity IDs.

sections.name: detection_profiles
sections.notes: All active fields emitted by the current detection-profile saver are typed, editable, and structurally creatable as a complete payload. Stable unreferenced profiles support confirmed structural deletion.

sections.name: captures
sections.notes: All active capture fields are typed and editable. Numeric quotas accept the full lossless JSON integer range supported by the GUI transport. Paths, filename components, destination addresses, and interface names use write-only replace/clear controls and remain redacted in draft responses.

sections.name: content_profiles
sections.notes: Content controls and nested rule action metadata are typed. Complete parent profiles support structural creation. Session filters and rule match/replacement expressions remain server-side and use write-only rotation. Stable unreferenced profiles support confirmed structural deletion. Nested rules support ordered structural creation, confirmed deletion, and first/before/last moves when the reviewed structural capability is available; their parent editor presents the effective draft order, labels pending moves and deletes, and permits create or move references to earlier same-parent pending creates. Accepted write-only create values are cleared from the editor and must be re-entered before updating a pending create operation.

sections.name: tls_ca
sections.notes: Authority names and path posture are exposed. Authorities support structural creation and confirmed deletion, with pending deletion labeled in the trust-asset list. Filesystem paths use write-only controls, are cleared after acceptance, remain redacted in draft responses, and must be re-entered before a pending create can be updated.

sections.name: tls_profiles
sections.notes: All active fields saved by the current Smithproxy TLS profile schema are typed, editable, and structurally creatable with conservative defaults. SNI bypass expressions support write-only replace or clear, are cleared after acceptance, and never cross the browser boundary. Updating a pending create requires explicit bypass-list re-entry. Stable unreferenced profiles support confirmed structural deletion.

sections.name: ssh_profiles
sections.notes: All active SSH profile fields are typed, editable, and structurally creatable with fail-closed defaults; host-key paths are write-only and remain redacted. Stable unreferenced profiles support confirmed structural deletion.

sections.name: alg_dns_profiles
sections.notes: The current DNS ALG profile schema is represented by typed edit and complete structural create drawers. Stable unreferenced profiles support confirmed structural deletion.

sections.name: routing
sections.notes: All active fields emitted by the current routing-profile saver are typed, editable, and structurally creatable with bounded unique destination lists. Address and port references resolve current draft-visible names while preserving stable live entity IDs. Stable unreferenced profiles support confirmed structural deletion.

sections.name: policy
sections.notes: All fields currently returned by the policy snapshot contract are represented by typed edit and ordered structural create drawers. Empty source, source-port, destination, and destination-port selectors preserve Smithproxy wildcard semantics. New action, NAT, and feature writes are constrained to the pinned Smithproxy enums; non-canonical legacy live values remain readable and can be migrated without resubmitting them when another field changes. References resolve live entities by their current draft-visible names and named objects or profiles created earlier in the same workspace draft; pending creates reopen their structural drawer and pending renames retain the stable live entity ID. Ordered creates and moves may target earlier pending policies through transaction-scoped client identifiers while use-before-create choices remain unavailable. Existing policies support optimistic first, before, and last move operations; restoring the original position removes the pending move. Confirmed structural deletion rejects conflicting pending field edits. Structural operations remain capability-gated on stable entity IDs.

sections.name: starttls_signatures
sections.notes: All active signature metadata and ordered flow controls are typed. Parent metadata and the required first flow step support atomic structural creation and linked removal with one draft version increment. Existing signatures support confirmed structural deletion and label that state in the trust-asset list. Matcher expressions remain server-side and support write-only replacement. Stable flow steps support ordered structural creation, confirmed deletion, and first/before/last moves when the reviewed structural capability is available; their parent editor presents the effective draft order, labels pending moves and deletes, and permits create or move references to earlier same-parent pending creates. Accepted write-only create values are cleared from the editor and must be re-entered before updating a pending create operation.

sections.name: detection_signatures
sections.notes: All active signature metadata and ordered flow controls are typed. Parent metadata and the required first flow step support atomic structural creation and linked removal with one draft version increment. Existing signatures support confirmed structural deletion and label that state in the trust-asset list. Matcher expressions remain server-side and support write-only replacement. Stable flow steps support ordered structural creation, confirmed deletion, and first/before/last moves when the reviewed structural capability is available; their parent editor presents the effective draft order, labels pending moves and deletes, and permits create or move references to earlier same-parent pending creates. Accepted write-only create values are cleared from the editor and must be re-entered before updating a pending create operation.

sections.name: script_profiles
sections.notes: All active script-profile fields are typed, editable, and structurally creatable; executable paths are write-only and remain redacted. Stable unreferenced profiles support confirmed structural deletion.

sections.name: auth_profiles
sections.notes: Authentication posture is typed and structurally creatable. Identity mappings for stable and pending-created profiles remain redacted, while complete replacements and clearing use a nested write-only editor with typed detection, content, TLS, and DNS profile bindings. Pending creates may reference compatible profiles created earlier in the same workspace draft. Accepted values are cleared from browser state, draft responses expose only the redacted operation and item count, and any later update requires complete re-entry. The GUI core privately resolves live and pending identity bindings into a complete effective reverse index, then erases their names before browser serialization. Draft responses expose only bounded opaque profile IDs with counts and an exact-revision completeness marker, so valid atomic cleanup is available without weakening deletion guards after reload. Profiles with effective hidden references reject rename until the complete mapping is replaced or cleared. Stable effectively unreferenced profiles support confirmed structural deletion.
